Online Video Tools That Run in Your Browser

Trim, crop, compress, convert or check a video without uploading it. Start with what needs to change, then open the tool and verify the saved file before sharing.

What needs to change in your video?

Edit the picturePrepare the fileHandle the audioCheck the file

Trim, join or crop the picture

  • Trim a time range when you need to remove the opening or ending. Set the start and end of the segment to keep.
  • Join clips in order when several videos need one MP4. If parts of the clips should be removed, trim those clips before joining.
  • Crop to portrait, square or landscape when the frame shape needs to change. Preview the crop through the whole clip to catch a moving subject that leaves the frame.
  • Save one frame as PNG for a still image or make a GIF from a short segment for an image loop without audio.

Meet a file-size or format requirement

Compress the video if an upload requires a smaller file. Trim and crop first if those edits are also needed. After compression, compare the saved size with the upload limit and play the file through to the end.

Convert to MP4 or WebM if the destination requires a different format. Try MP4 with H.264 and AAC when the app expects those codecs. If your original already meets the size limit, keep it while testing compatibility.

Check, remove or save the sound

  • Check the audio track if the video sounds silent. An absent track calls for a different fix from a track with very quiet or zero samples.
  • Remove all audio tracks to make a silent file. The compatible video track is copied without another picture encode.
  • Save the soundtrack separately before removing it if you need it later. Copy an AAC track to M4A or decode it to WAV when supported.

Unsure which edit the video needs?

Open the saved file and compare it with the destination’s requirements. Check what must change first.

  • Duration or frame shape. Check the length and watch the subject through the whole clip. Trim for duration and crop for framing. A centered crop can remove important details at the edges.
  • File size or format. Compare the saved bytes with the limit and check the required format. Try a short export before re-encoding a long video.
  • Sound. Confirm whether the output should contain a track at all. A video that sounds quiet can still contain an audio track.

Save each intermediate file until the final file passes playback and format checks. Edits run on your device. Browser codec support, track count and available memory affect which files each tool can open. For a Canva export, follow the MP4 download and export checks first.

Make a short vertical MP4 with no audio track

Use this four-second sample with a tone to try the tools in sequence.

  1. In Trim Video, keep seconds 1 to 3 and download the result.
  2. Open that file in the cropper, choose Portrait · 9:16, leave the crop centered and save another MP4. Preview movement at both ends before applying the same workflow to your own clip.
  3. Open the cropped file in Mute Video and save the silent MP4. Verify that the last file still plays and that the audio checker reports No audio track found.

In the tested run, the source was 640 × 360 with one audio track. Trimming produced a 2.008-second clip. The final file measured 198 × 352 pixels, 2 seconds and zero audio tracks. Download the final example or check the measured output at each step.
